surprises.description: JetBlue recaptured 87% of higher Q3 fuel costs, well above the preview’s threshold of 60% for a meaningful improvement to the 2027 outlook. The preview had highlighted fuel recapture as a key risk amid the fuel-price shock.
surprises.fact_evidence: “JetBlue recaptured 87% of higher fuel costs in Q3.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q3 recapture above 60% would materially change the 2027 bridge.”

surprises.description: JetBlue reported $2.2 billion in liquidity and roughly $7 billion in unencumbered assets, versus the preview’s base-case liquidity estimate of $1.9–2.0 billion and its roughly $6 billion unencumbered-asset estimate. The preview’s central concern was whether the balance sheet and collateral could withstand the fuel shock.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company ended Q3 with $2.2 billion in liquidity (including a $600 million undrawn revolver) and roughly $7 billion in unencumbered assets,” including “$2.8 billion in aircraft and engines (up from ~$2 billion).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The base scenario anticipated “liquidity ~$1.9–2.0B”; the preview also cited a “claimed ~$6B unencumbered asset base.”

surprises.description: JetBlue forecast Q4 RASM growth of 18% to 22% and a fifth consecutive quarter of accelerating RASM. That reaches the preview’s 18% threshold for a strong Q4 guide, though it remains below the preview’s estimate that roughly 24% growth was needed to hold the operating line flat against fuel alone.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 RASM growth of 18% to 22% year-over-year, marking an expected fifth consecutive quarter of accelerating RASM.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Q4 needs ~+24% RASM just to hold the operating line flat on fuel alone”; “anything below ~+18% confirms recapture is topping out.”

surprises.description: Despite the preview’s concern that Q4 would bring a wider loss as fuel costs rose, JetBlue guided to 1 to 2 points of year-over-year Q4 operating-margin expansion. That is a more favorable margin outlook, although the reported comparison is year over year rather than sequentially.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q4 is expected to deliver 1 to 2 points of year-over-year margin expansion.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Expect a Q4 guide implying a wider loss than Q3.”

surprises.description: Q3 CASM ex-fuel rose 7%, but JetBlue attributed about 4 points to summer disruption and forecast Q4 CASM ex-fuel between -1% and +1%. This supports the preview’s transitory-disruption possibility rather than a persistently high cost trend.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 CASM ex-fuel rose 7% year-over-year including ~4 points of summer disruption pressure, with Q4 guided to between negative 1% and positive 1%.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “watch whether this is transitory deleverage or structural.”

surprises.description: Management reaffirmed the 2027 profitability target and also set out a longer-range goal of at least $1 of EPS and positive free cash flow in 2028, conditional on fuel assumptions. The preview focused on the 2027 commitment and did not flag a 2028 target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management reaffirmed targets of sustained operating profitability in 2027 and at least $1 of EPS plus positive free cash flow in 2028,” assuming fuel slightly above $4 in 2027 and around $3 in 2028.

surprises.description: Fort Lauderdale posted nearly 15% RASM growth while capacity there increased more than 65%, with further seat-share and departure growth planned. The preview did not discuss this market-specific expansion, which also differs from its broader description of an industry prioritizing margins over volume.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Fort Lauderdale RASM grew nearly 15% year-over-year on more than 65% capacity growth in Q3,” with seat share expected to reach about 37% in Q4 and peak daily departures exceeding 150 this winter.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview described the industry as “prioritizing margins over volume.”

surprises.description: JetBlue reported 20% loyalty-revenue growth and an eightfold year-over-year increase in Premier Card acquisitions. The preview highlighted TrueBlue’s role in the debt-service covenant but did not anticipate this growth in loyalty activity.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Loyalty revenue grew 20% in Q3 (highest since 2023), Premier Card acquisitions grew eightfold year-over-year.”

surprises.description: Paisly was on track to produce nearly $100 million in operating income this year, with that amount expected to nearly double by 2028—an earnings contribution and growth outlook not discussed in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Paisly is on track for nearly $100 million in operating income this year, expected to nearly double by 2028.”

surprises.description: Blue First had launched across more than 30 routes, with about 35% of bookings as award redemptions, but fleet installation will not finish until late 2028 because of supply-chain constraints. The preview did not address the product; the reported redemption uptake is encouraging, while the extended rollout is a constraint.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Blue First domestic first-class launched December 8 across 30+ routes with ~35% of bookings as award redemptions”; installation “will largely complete in 2027 but not finish until late 2028 due to supply chain constraints.”
